weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg2:start is a plain stacked 68/32 column whose 32% label nearly disappears. seg2:mid and seg2:end switch to two bare vertical poles on an axis captioned '36% apart', with the two share labels crowded above the bracket and most of the frame empty.
weakest_scene.root_cause: A share-of-a-whole claim (68% of residents live in the hottest pockets) was routed to a stock gap-gauge machine. The gauge treats the two parts of one whole as two separate measurements, so the '36% apart' headline says nothing the narration claims, and the gauge's thin layout leaves the frame empty.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Show 68% as people in a city: a block of 100 resident figures or rooftops where 68 turn heat-red under treeless, paved squares and 32 stay cool under trees. Data walks into the hot section. Drop the '36% apart' gap framing, put every label in high-contrast ink, and fill the frame.
